Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
14 October 2026 .
Brent $ 106.11 + 0.69 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 Reuters reports Iran is shifting tactics to intensify attacks on shipping before the US vote, per officials, a story also carried by The Diplomatic Insight.

02 The Maritime Executive reports two more ship strikes in the Strait of Hormuz; TradeWinds News reports UKMTO says a tanker and a container ship were attacked in the strait, reported October 12.

03 Brent stood at $106.11, up 0.69% over 24 hours, as of 06:12 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains the center of an intensifying attack campaign against commercial shipping. The lead development in this window is Reuters reporting, citing officials, that Iran is shifting tactics to step up attacks on shipping before the US vote, a story The Diplomatic Insight also carries. The Maritime Executive reports two additional ship strikes in the strait. TradeWinds News reports that UKMTO says a tanker and a container ship were attacked in the strait; that report was filed October 12, and no row in this window states when those strikes occurred or names the vessels, so they are treated as distinct from the two strikes The Maritime Executive covers only if a ship name or position sets them apart, which none does here. Separately, Anadolu Ajansı reports a tanker caught fire east of the strait, with no major wire in this feed independently carrying that claim. On the diplomatic track, no headline in this window carries new detail on the status of Iran's response to Washington's reply to its seven conditions. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent stood at $106.11, up 0.69% over 24 hours, as of 06:12 UTC. The feed indexed 47 headlines in the last 24 hours across the crisis. As of 06:22 UTC, 93 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
